article_lead.description: a variance-based bound on large deviations from the mean that works without assuming a distributional shape

new_bank_questions.title: A sample size from Chebyshev's bound
new_bank_questions.body: Independent observations have population variance 25. How many are needed so that Chebyshev's inequality guarantees P(|sample mean - population mean|≥1)≤0.05? State why the calculation could fail for correlated observations.
new_bank_questions.answer: For n independent observations, Var(sample mean)=25/n and Chebyshev bounds the probability by 25/n. Requiring 25/n≤0.05 gives n≥500. Correlation changes the variance of the average, so the 25/n formula may fail.
